name: connection.hello
description: Handshake. First verb on a new connection; required before any other verb is accepted. From v2.2 onwards the response body is mandatory and carries the negotiated framing — clients consume the OK body fully and then switch to that framing for every subsequent message on the connection.

client_version.description: Protocol version the client wishes to speak, e.g. '2.2'. Server picks the highest mutually-supported version and echoes it in the response's `agent_protocol` field. v2.2+ agents do NOT advertise v2.1 as supported — v2.1 clients receive `ERR protocol_mismatch` and must upgrade.

client_name.description: Free-form client identifier echoed in the agent's session log (e.g. "claude-code", "conformance", "my-llm-rig"). Optional; defaults to an empty string when omitted. Useful for log correlation on multi-client agents.

framing.description: Wire framing for this connection. When omitted: defaults to 'mcp' on a v2.2+ negotiated session; v2.1 clients are rejected with `ERR protocol_mismatch` (no v2.1 backward compat in v2.2+ agents). 'mcp' = MCP-stdio framing (`Content-Length: N\r\n\r\n<JSON>`) carrying MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 messages, active after this OK body is consumed. 'ws' = RFC 6455 binary frames (FIN=1, opcode 0x02, client-masked) carrying the same MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 body, also active after this OK body is consumed; no HTTP upgrade — the framing change is in-protocol. Both available on `windows-modern` only; `windows-classic` returns `ERR framing_unsupported`. Added v2.2.

protocol.description: Protocol identifier — always the literal "arh" (Agent Remote Hands). Lets clients verify the wire protocol upfront.

agent_protocol.description: Wire-protocol version this agent speaks for this connection, e.g. "2.2". The negotiated highest mutually-supported version. Mirrors `system.info.agent_protocol`.

os_name.description: Human-readable OS product name, e.g. "Windows 11 Pro". Mirrors `system.info.os_name`.

session_id.description: Fresh per-connection identifier for log correlation; opaque to the client.

framing.description: Wire framing active on this connection from the byte immediately following this OK body. 'mcp' = MCP-stdio framing carrying MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 (default for v2.2+). 'ws' = RFC 6455 binary frames carrying the same body shape. Always present on a v2.2+ session — clients use this field to confirm which framing the agent has selected before switching their parser. Added v2.2.

x-implementations.name: agent_native
x-implementations.description: Handled inline by the agent's wire-framing / lifecycle layer. No OS-level backend; no fallback possible.

windows-modern.description: Agent-internal lifecycle verb; no Windows-specific behaviour. The handshake runs in the agent's framing thread before any OS call. Honours `--framing mcp` (default for v2.2+) and `--framing ws`; both are advertised in `system.info.framings`. Returns `ERR framing_unsupported` for any other value.

windows-classic.description: Agent-internal lifecycle verb; no Windows-specific behaviour. The handshake runs in the agent's framing thread before any OS call. `--framing ws` and `--framing mcp` always return `ERR framing_unsupported` on classic — the family stays on the v2.0 / v2.1 ARH header-line wire format, which is also used as the bootstrap framing on modern. `system.info.framings` therefore reports an empty / single-entry list on classic.
